REVISEThe central fixed-region combinatorial argument is largely correct, but the theorem package is not correct as written. There are two material construction/definition problems and one scope problem:the reservation rule does not consistently imply  $|F|=D-2L$ ;the geometry does not imply the two-witness minimum degree required by the Hall argument;the first “private repair” staircase construction is infeasible under the stated coordinates and matching direction.The multigraph component accounting, the parity deduction, the one-witness obstruction, and the parallel-edge treatment are sound after the reservation and source-domain statements are repaired.1. Reservation count: equation (1) needs a precise policyLet
$$n_1=\#\{U\subseteq R: U\text{ deficient and }t(U)=1\}.$$
Since a deficient tile has  $t\in\{0,1\}$ ,
$$\sum_{\text{deficient }U\subseteq R} b(U)=D+n_1.$$
To obtain
$$|F|=D-2L,$$
the total number of distinct reserved blank vertices must be exactly
$$n_1+2L.$$
The intended counting is presumably:one baseline blank in every  $t=1$  deficient tile:  $n_1$  blanks;two cap blanks in every marked tile:  $2L$  blanks;with all these sets pairwise disjoint.Then
$$|F|=(D+n_1)-n_1-2L=D-2L.$$
However, the wording currently says:Reserve one internal blank neighbor of the  $T$  in every deficient tile with  $t=1$ .In a marked tile with  $t=1$ , reserve the other noncap corner.Reserve the two cap blanks as well.These reservations are disjoint.Read literally, this reserves an additional “other noncap corner” after the baseline internal neighbor and after the two cap blanks. That gives too many reservations. A marked  $t=1$  tile has at most three non- $T$  corners. Since  $b-t\ge 2$  and  $t=1$ , it must have  $b=3$  and  $p=0$ . Four pairwise-distinct blank reservations in that tile are impossible.There is a second issue in the sentenceAny such choice of the noncap  $T$  reservations is permitted.For a marked  $t=1$  tile, the baseline blank must be chosen carefully. If the arbitrary internal blank chosen is one of the cap blanks, then the baseline and cap reservations overlap. The claimed disjointness fails, and equation (1) no longer follows.The repair is straightforward but must be stated explicitly:for every unmarked  $t=1$  tile, choose any one internal blank neighbor;for every marked  $t=1$  tile, choose the pressure-forced other noncap corner as that one baseline reservation;require this corner to be outside the two cap blanks;do not count it as an additional reservation.With that policy, the reservation count is correct. Without it, the definition of  $F$ , and therefore every later identity involving  $F$ , is not well-defined.2. The degree-two multiplicity bound is correctFor a blank  $x\in F$  at a corner of its deficient tile, two of its four grid neighbors are internal to that tile. Only the two external orthogonal neighbors can be selected corners of saturated tiles. Those external neighbors lie in two different neighboring tiles. Therefore
$$\deg_F(x)\le 2.$$
This correctly treats the witness relation as a physical incidence relation. Different orientation descriptions that refer to the same blank do not create multiple edges. Conversely, two distinct blanks connecting the same pair of saturated owners do create two distinct parallel edges, and must remain distinct.This part is sound.3. The Hall payment is correct only under an explicit left-degree hypothesisThe Hall argument is valid under the stated condition
$$\deg_F(S)\ge 2\qquad\text{for every }S\in A.$$
Indeed, for  $X\subseteq A$ , the incidence count gives
$$2|X|
   \le \sum_{x\in N(X)}\deg_A(x)
   \le 2|N(X)|,$$
so  $|N(X)|\ge |X|$ , and Hall supplies an injection  $A\hookrightarrow F$ .The alternating-path proof is also correct.What does not follow from the geometry is the left-degree assumption  $\deg_F(S)\ge2$ . The geometry shows that a saturated attachment has up to four forced external blanks. It does not show that two of those blanks:lie inside  $R$ ;belong to deficient tiles;remain in  $F$  after reservation;are not on the grid boundary;or are not in saturated tiles.Thus the statementThis derives the required allocation condition from grid geometryis too strong. Geometry supplies the right-degree bound, but the two-witness lower bound must remain an explicit hypothesis or certificate.A simple feasible configuration already shows the issue. Let  $R$  contain a saturated tile  $S$  and a deficient tile  $W$  to its right:
$$S:\quad
\begin{array}{c|c}
T & P\\
B & T
\end{array},
\qquad
W:\quad
\begin{array}{c|c}
P & P\\
B & P
\end{array}.$$
Match the  $P$  at  $S$ 's upper-right corner to  $W$ 's upper-left corner, and match the other two  $P$ 's of  $W$  to vertices outside  $R$ . The blank at  $W$ 's lower-left corner is one forced witness for  $S$ ; the other forced neighbors of  $S$ 's selected corners are outside  $R$ . Hence  $S$  has only one neighbor in  $F$ .All  $T$ -constraints and the no-saturated-to-saturated condition can be satisfied. Therefore the Hall theorem is a valid conditional lemma, but not an unconditional consequence of the local tile geometry.The later component theorem is precisely what is needed to handle degree-zero and degree-one attachments. The document should present the two-witness result as a sufficient special case, not as a condition automatically forced by the grid.4. The parity improvement is algebraically correctAssuming the stated ledger identities and the valid lower bound  $D\ge 2L+k$ , let
$$\varepsilon=(j+\eta)\bmod 2.$$
From
$$D\equiv j+Q\equiv j+k+\eta\pmod 2,$$
we obtain
$$D-(2L+k)\equiv j+\eta\equiv \varepsilon\pmod2.$$
Therefore
$$D\ge 2L+k+\varepsilon,$$
and hence
$$2\rho(R)
=-D+k+\sigma
\le -2L+\sigma-\varepsilon.$$
So equation (3) is correct once equation (1) and the allocation lower bound are valid.5. The component identities are correct for one global witness graphWith one fixed region  $R$ , one fixed reservation policy, and one global witness graph, define: $v=k$ ; $e$  = number of degree-two witness blanks; $p$  = number of degree-one witness blanks; $u$  = number of degree-zero blanks in  $F$ ; $c$  = number of connected components of  $H$ , including isolated attachment vertices; $\mu=e-v+c$ .Then
$$|F|=e+p+u$$
and
$$k-|F|
=v-(e+p+u)
=c-\mu-p-u.$$
Combining this with
$$2\rho(R)=-D+k+\sigma,
\qquad
D=2L+|F|,$$
gives
$$2\rho(R)
=-2L+\sigma+c-\mu-p-u.$$
Equation (4) is therefore correct under the repaired definition of  $F$ .The allocation characterization is also correct for the loop-free multigraph supplied by the grid:a component with a private blank can be rooted at that private blank;a component containing a cycle can assign cycle blanks cyclically and attach trees outward;a tree with no private blank has  $v-1$  blanks for  $v$  owners and leaves exactly one owner unmatched.The grid geometry gives distinct owners for the two external neighbors of an  $F$ -blank, so loops do not arise. That loop-free condition should nevertheless be stated when presenting the abstract multigraph theorem.Parallel edges are essential. In the cycle repair, the original blank  $W_i.\mathrm{TL}$  and the newly added blank  $V.\mathrm{BR}$  are two different physical vertices joining the same owner pair. They produce two parallel edges and increase  $\mu$  by one. Collapsing them to a simple edge would incorrectly report a tree with one unmatched owner.6. The source-region statement and equation (5) are under-specifiedFor one fixed  $R$ , equation (4) immediately implies the weaker inequality
$$2\rho(R)\le \sigma+c-\mu-p-u$$
because  $L\ge0$ . That is the only conclusion currently justified directly.The phrasedisjoint sources of total charge at most  $L$ is not defined precisely enough to support the displayed statement involving  $R\cup\text{sources}$ . If  $R\cup\text{sources}$  is a genuinely larger region, then  $D,k,\sigma,F,H,c,\mu,p,u$  must all be recomputed for that union. One cannot simply reuse the values from the original  $R$ .There is also a real resource-reuse hazard if source regions are analyzed separately. A single physical blank can be adjacent to two saturated owners. If two local source analyses each treat that blank as a private witness, their separate allocations can both consume the same physical vertex. The correct procedure is either:prove that the  $F$ -sets of the source regions are disjoint and that no attachment/witness crosses the source boundaries; orform one global witness graph on the union and apply the multigraph criterion once.The sentence “Each blank has one identity in this sum” is correct only after such a global partition or global graph has been defined. It does not by itself justify summing independently constructed local allocations.Thus equation (5) should be rewritten with an explicit definition of the source family, disjointness of physical tile and blank sets, and the treatment of boundary attachments. The assertion  $\sigma=0$  also requires a closure condition; it is not automatic merely from saying that the sources are disjoint.7. The staircase without repair is validThe no-repair staircase calculations check out.For  $W_0$ ,
$$t=0,\quad b=1,\quad h=0,\quad s=2,\quad d=1,$$
so
$$r=2-t-h-s=0,
\qquad
\rho(W_0)=\frac12.$$
For  $i\ge1$ ,
$$t=0,\quad b=1,\quad h=1,\quad s=1,\quad d=0,$$
so  $\rho(W_i)=0$ .Therefore
$$D=a-1,\qquad k=a,\qquad \sigma=\eta=0,\qquad j=1,\qquad Q=a,$$
and
$$2\rho(R)=-D+k=1.$$
The  $a-1$  free blanks  $W_i.\mathrm{TL}$  give a path on the  $a$  saturated owners:
$$c=1,\qquad \mu=0,\qquad p=0,\qquad u=0.$$
It is therefore impossible to assign distinct blanks to all  $a$  attachments. This correctly refutes the naive “one witness per attachment is enough” rule. It does not constitute a counterexample to the whole-grid target, as the document correctly acknowledges.8. The cycle repair is valid; the private repair is not valid as writtenThe second repair, with  $V=(1,a-1)$ , is consistent with the intended geometry. Its blank  $V.\mathrm{BR}$  is adjacent to the selected corners of  $S_0$  and  $S_1$ , creating a second physical edge between those owners. Together with the original  $W_0.\mathrm{TL}$  edge, these form a two-edge parallel cycle. Thus
$$\mu=1,$$
and the added tile's charge  $-\tfrac12$  cancels the original  $\tfrac12$  debt. This repair works for every  $a\ge2$ , subject to making the coordinate orientation explicit.The first repair is inconsistent with the stated coordinates and matching direction.The relevant tile data are:tileTLTRBLBR $S_0$  $B$  $T$  $T$  $P$  $V$  $P$  $P$  $P$  $B$ Because  $V=(0,a)$  and  $S_0=(1,a)$ ,  $V$  is immediately to the left of  $S_0$  in the coordinate arrangement used by the staircase. This is also forced by the assertion that  $V.\mathrm{BR}$  is private to  $S_0$ : that corner is adjacent to  $S_0.\mathrm{BL}$ .But then the “immediate right external neighbor” of  $V.\mathrm{TR}$  is  $S_0.\mathrm{TL}$ . Matching
$$V.\mathrm{TR}\;-\;S_0.\mathrm{TL}$$
turns  $S_0.\mathrm{TL}$  into a  $P$ -vertex. The  $T$  at  $S_0.\mathrm{TR}$  then has two occupied neighbors,  $S_0.\mathrm{TL}$  and  $S_0.\mathrm{BR}$ . This violates the basic feasibility condition, and  $S_0$  also acquires two  $P$ -corners, contradicting the saturated-tile fact.So repair 1 is not a feasible pair under the written coordinates. Its claimed charge  $-\tfrac12$  and its objective value cannot be used until the matching direction or tile placement is changed. For example, one could match  $V.\mathrm{TR}$  to an actually external non- $S_0$  neighbor, but that is a different construction and must be rechecked.Required revisionsTo make the theorem auditable and potentially acceptable:Define the baseline  $t=1$  reservation and the cap reservations as disjoint sets explicitly.In marked  $t=1$  tiles, make the pressure-forced other noncap corner the single baseline reservation; do not reserve it again.Remove the assertion that an arbitrary internal blank choice is allowed in marked  $t=1$  tiles.State the Hall theorem with  $\deg_F(S)\ge2$  as a hypothesis, or explicitly invoke the later component criterion when that condition fails.Define “source region,” “total charge,” and the exact disjointness conditions needed for source summation.Use one global witness graph whenever source regions can share or cross witness incidences.Correct the first staircase repair or remove it from the claimed all- $a$  construction family.Keep the multigraph, rather than its simple-graph quotient, so parallel physical blanks remain separate resources.With these changes, the fixed-region distinct-blank allocation theorem and the staircase obstruction can be accepted as sound conditional results. The document in its current form should be marked REVISE, not ACCEPT.
